newsitem.title: UK: Major accuses Labour of effrontery over economy.
newsitem.headline: Major accuses Labour of effrontery over economy.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major on Tuesday accused the opposition Labour Party of "an astonishing piece of brass-necked effrontery" in claiming it could run the British economy more effectively than his own government has.
Speaking to party workers and pensioners at a meeting in Brighton, southern England, Major said that when Labour gave up power in 1979 Britain had had a "basket case economy".
Over the past 18 years this had been transformed into the best performing economy in Europe, he said.
"All the things we did to achieve it they (Labour) stood against and opposed," Major said.

He accused Labour leader Tony Blair of "truly unscrupulous untruths" in claiming that the Conservatives would put value added tax on food and scrap the state pension if they were returned to power on May 1.
"I believe they have truly stepped into the gutter of public life," Major said.
"We Conservatives and the British nation built that (successful) economy. The Labour Party would not be able to sustain it."
